Convert a PDF

Convert a Scanned PDF to Markdown on Mac

Run the local Swift converter to keep existing PDF text and OCR image-only pages with Apple Vision. It writes one Markdown section per page. If a page has selectable text and a scanned image, you can choose that page for OCR explicitly.

  1. Convert a PDF on macOS
  2. Choose specific pages for OCR
  3. Check page coverage and reading order
  4. Try a known sample

Extract text and OCR image-only pages on Mac

Download the Swift converter. If your Mac does not have swift, install Apple’s Command Line Tools with xcode-select --install. The converter uses macOS PDFKit and Apple Vision after that setup.

Run this from the folder with the script and PDF. Pick a new output path. The converter refuses to replace an existing file.

swift pdf-to-markdown.swift "scan.pdf" "scan.md"

The converter reads extractable text where it can and applies English OCR to pages whose text layer is empty. Both modes write a page heading, the extraction method and the recovered text into the same Markdown file. The PDF stays on your Mac.

What text can you select in the PDF?

Run OCRChoose pagesVerify the text

OCR a specific page that is missing scanned text

A page can have a selectable header and still contain an image with the text you need. When you spot a missing sentence in the Markdown, use the PDF viewer’s physical page position and rerun to a new filename.

swift pdf-to-markdown.swift "scan.pdf" "scan-rechecked.md" --ocr-pages 3,5

Replace 3,5 with the pages you want to read as images. On those pages, OCR supplies the entire page’s text. Keep the first Markdown for comparison. For text-based tables, try the MarkItDown table check before replacing the text-layer result with OCR.

Check the Markdown page by page

  1. Search for a known phrase from each important page. Compare the exact spellings, numbers, decimal points, units and IDs with the PDF.
  2. If you see No text recovered, open that page in the PDF viewer. A blank page may be expected. A nonblank page might need a clearer scan or another OCR language.
  3. Check tables and columns for reading order. The output stores page text in fenced blocks. For AI search, confirm your importer indexes the block and captures its source page. A useful retrieval test asks for a value that only the scanned page contains.

The scan mode is configured for English printed text. Handwriting, complex layouts and scanned text in other languages need separate verification. Unlock password-protected documents before trying the script.

Try the three-page sample

Download the synthetic support PDF and run the converter. Pages 1 and 2 should use the PDF text layer. Page 3 should use OCR and recover SCAN-43 and 72 hours. In our trial, forcing OCR on page 2 changed the reading order of the table cells. Keep the original table as the reference.

Download the default output, compare the forced OCR output or read the checks. Tests ran on macOS 26.4.1, Apple M4, with outbound internet access denied. The sample is a printed, single-column scan with a separate text-based table page.

See Apple’s Vision text recognition guide and PDFKit page reference.
